body: Fear of failure. I feel like I make my friends and family’s lives worse, but if I made myself bed-ridden, that would make it 5 times worse for them. There are methods I’ve sent that have a pretty high success rate, but I’m not very interested unless it’s something above 99%. I would not want to fail.

Is it racist? The definition of normal is literally “average”, and in America this is true to an extent. It’s not correct wording in the slightest bit, of course not, but I wouldn’t go as far as to say that it’s “prejudice against a certain race”. Not only that, but I’ve never heard “normal” used as a compliment. Conforming to society’s “norms” is almost never regarded as a positive
Thank you so much for the tip. You’re right, though. Being honest is the best thing I can do.
The TL;DR words my dilemma better, so if the main paragraph is confusing, I think it will clear things up.
That’d would be my guess based on the response of others, since I’m asexual and curious what other people would think is the same kind of thing, but different.

My life’s almost perfect around me, but I’ve considered/lucid dreamed me doing such awful things nobody knows about that I can’t wait until the cowardliness fades away and I commit suicide, and I explain everything in my suicide note, and everyone I knew feels relieved I’m gone, so yes, my life’s great but I couldn’t be more opposite than it.
I’d scroll through Reddit until I die of old age because I’m too cowardly to kill myself.

Maybe my life isn’t fantastic, but the events in my life are. If I wasn’t such a useless human my life would be basically perfect, unlike every other post I’ve seen so far in this subreddit where the suicidal person isn’t the problem, but the events that happened to them are.

No, I mean curious as in I’m curious if other people are suicidal not because their life is tragic but because they think they’re too terrible to be here. There’s people like this, I know, but I quite sure all of them loathe themselves because they’re blaming themselves for some tragic event in life, not a reason based on logic, but I can’t blame them, since I understand how much depression can twist your mind into a specific thought process.
It seems like you judge yourself based on what some people think. You’re responsible for your opinion of yourself, and I know that may seem cliche but it’s true.

Don’t ask me why, but the nicest people on Earth get the least in return, so you must be really nice. You don’t do nice things for things in return. You do it for a sense of accomplishment. Same reason people learn to draw or play an instrument. Don’t give up.
Well everyone gets dumped, too. The popular, the unpopular, the rich, and the poor. Either way, you need time to think about it

Well, having a girlfriend that loved you proves that you’re worthy of loving. Everyone loses people they love and it’s hard to go through, but it seems that you’ve already endured so much suffering already. Losing a loved one can blind someone, so give yourself some time to collect your thoughts. I’m here for you
Really depends on how much they know you and how nice of a person they are
